title: Using a nebulizer
what: A nebulizer turns liquid medicine into a fine mist. You breathe it in calmly through a mask or mouthpiece.
why: For bronchitis with shortness of breath, asthma, croup in children, and other lung conditions, as your doctor prescribes.
tell_doctor: If you get a racing heart or shaking after a treatment
If the treatments are not helping

prepare.title: Medicine
prepare.text: Use only what your doctor prescribed, at that dose. Dilute it with saline, usually. Do not use tap water.

prepare.title: Timing
prepare.text: Usually at least an hour after a meal.

prepare.title: Device
prepare.text: Read the nebulizer instructions before the first use.

bring: Your nebulizer and mask or mouthpiece
steps: Pour the medicine into the nebulizer cup
Attach the mask or mouthpiece and turn the device on
Sit up straight and breathe calmly through your mouth
Keep breathing until the mist stops
Turn off the device. After steroid medicines, rinse your mouth
feel: Some medicines can cause a racing heart or slightly shaky hands
after: Rinse the cup and mask with warm water and let them dry
Clean the parts regularly, as the instructions say
Do not put oils, herbs, or herbal teas in a nebulizer
red_flags: Shortness of breath gets worse, it is hard to talk, or lips turn blue: call emergency services
A child has a barking cough with noisy breathing that does not get better after the treatment: call emergency services

faq.q: Can I use mineral water in the nebulizer?
faq.a: Only if your doctor said so. Saline is usually used to dilute medicines.

faq.q: Can I use it with a fever?
faq.a: Usually yes, if your doctor prescribed it. Hot steam inhalations are different. They are not done with a fever.

reminders.text: Time for your nebulizer. Use the prescribed medicine, breathe calmly through your mouth, then rinse the mask.
